text: Visible faces, horizon edges, perturbation.

The 3D convex hull (三维凸包) is made of triangular faces. Incremental construction: start with a tetrahedron, then add points one by one. A face is visible from the new point p if p lies on its outer side (positive triple product). Delete all visible faces; the edges on the border between visible and invisible faces (the "horizon") each form a new face with p. O(n²) total, enough for n ≤ 2000 (P4724).

Mark visibility per directed edge: for each face (a, b, c) visible from p, set vis[a][b] = vis[b][c] = vis[c][a]. An edge (a, b) of a kept face with vis[b][a] set is a horizon edge, and the new face is (a, b, p) with the same orientation. Perturb the points by about 10⁻⁹ first, so that no four points are coplanar.

Four nested loops; circumsphere by elimination.

The minimum enclosing sphere (最小球覆盖) extends the random incremental circle of 拓展篇第15章 one level deeper: shuffle the points; whenever point i is outside the current sphere, restart with i on the boundary; inside that, whenever j is outside, restart with i and j on the boundary; then k; then l, where four boundary points fix the sphere. Expected O(n) after shuffling.
The sphere through 2 points: centre at the midpoint. Through 3: the circumcircle centre in their plane. Through 4: solve the 3 × 3 linear system |c − pi|² = |c − p0|² (Gaussian elimination, 进阶篇第22章).

The corners of a 4 × 4 × 4 cube plus interior points need the sphere of radius 2√3 (half the space diagonal); two points 10 apart need radius 5. Both answers are exact formulas, independent of the program.

Degenerate input (three collinear points, four coplanar points) makes circum3 / circum4 divide by zero; real solutions either perturb the points or check the determinant and fall back to the smaller case.
Merge edge lists by angle.

The Minkowski sum (闵可夫斯基和) A + B = {a + b} of two convex polygons is convex, and its edges are the edges of A and B sorted by angle. Start both at their lowest (then leftmost) vertex and merge the two edge lists like merge sort, comparing directions by cross product: O(n + m).

Typical uses: "can polygon B moved by vector v touch A?" ⇔ v ∈ A + (−B) (P4557 战争), distances between convex polygons, and motion planning. Remove collinear vertices afterwards if the problem wants a strict polygon.
Two random convex polygons, checked against the convex hull of all n·m pairwise sums in Python (same vertex count and doubled area).
Split until halves agree; union of circles.

Adaptive Simpson integration (自适应辛普森): Simpson's rule ∫lr f ≈ (r − l)(f(l) + 4f(m) + f(r)) / 6. Compare the whole interval with its two halves; if they agree within 15·ε accept, otherwise recurse on each half with ε / 2. The function only needs to be evaluable, not integrable by hand.

Classic use: the area of a union of circles (or other shapes) as ∫ f(x) dx, where f(x) = total length of the union of the vertical chords at x (merge intervals). Integrate each connected x-range separately (f = 0 in gaps fools the error test), and force a few levels of recursion before trusting the error estimate.

Five random circles, checked against an exact union area in Python (Green's theorem over the arcs not covered by other circles). The minimum depth 8 stops an early, lucky agreement on a coarse split.

Simpson assumes f is smooth; at chord ends f has √ cusps, which is why the adaptive version (not a fixed number of slices) is needed. ε too small makes it slow: pick it a few digits below the required precision.

Voronoi diagram and Delaunay triangulation (Voronoi 图 / Delaunay 三角剖分): the Voronoi cell of a site is the set of points nearest to it; joining sites whose cells share an edge gives the Delaunay triangulation (no point inside any triangle's circumcircle). Both have O(n) size and are built in O(n log n) (divide and conquer or Fortune's sweep). The Euclidean MST is a subgraph of the Delaunay triangulation.
They are rare in NOI; know them by name and use half-plane intersection (拓展篇) for small n.

Key points to memorise
1. Face visible from p: positive triple product.
2. Delete visible faces; horizon edge (visible one side only) + p ⇒ new face.
3. Perturb by ~1e-9 against coplanar points; O(n²).
4. Min sphere: shuffle; nested loops with 1, 2, 3, 4 boundary points; expected O(n).
5. Minkowski: start at lowest points, merge edges by cross product; O(n + m).
6. Adaptive Simpson: |L + R − S| ≤ 15ε ⇒ accept; integrate each x-component separately.
